chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنِ الْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid who said:

chunks.arabic_text: حَجَجْتُ وَسُكَيْنُ النَّخَعِيُّ فَتَعَبَّدَ وَتَرَكَ النِّسَاءَ وَالطِّيبَ وَالثِّيَابَ وَالطَّعَامَ الطَّيِّبَ وَكَانَ لَا يَرْفَعُ رَأْسَهُ دَاخِلَ الْمَسْجِدِ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَلَمَّا قَدِمَ الْمَدِينَةَ دَنَا مِنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ فَصَلَّى إِلَى جَانِبِهِ فَقَالَ: جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَكَ عَنْ مَسَائِلَ قَالَ: اذْهَبْ فَاكْتُبْهَا وَأَرْسِلْهَا إِلَيَّ، فَكَتَبَ: جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ رَجُلٌ دَخَلَهُ الْخَوْفُ مِنَ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ حَتَّى تَرَكَ النِّسَاءَ وَالطَّعَامَ الطَّيِّبَ وَلَا يَقْدِرُ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ رَأْسَهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَأَمَّا الثِّيَابُ فَشُكَّ فِيهَا، فَكَتَبَ: أَمَّا قَوْلُكَ فِي تَرْكِ النِّسَاءِ فَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا كَانَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ، وَأَمَّا قَوْلُكَ فِي تَرْكِ الطَّعَامِ الطَّيِّبِ فَقَدْ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَأْكُلُ اللَّحْمَ وَالْعَسَلَ، وَأَمَّا قَوْلُكَ إِنَّهُ دَخَلَهُ الْخَوْفُ حَتَّى لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ رَأْسَهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَلْيُكْثِرْ مِنْ تِلَاوَةِ هَذِهِ الْآيَاتِ: الصَّابِرِينَ وَالصَّادِقِينَ وَالْقَانِتِينَ وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالْأَسْحَارِ

translations.en: I made the Hajj with Sukayn al-Nakhai, and he devoted himself to worship and abandoned women, perfume, clothes, and good food, and he used not to raise his head inside the Masjid to the sky. When he arrived in Medina, he came near to Abu Ishaq and prayed by his side, then he said: May I be your ransom, I want to ask you about some matters. He said: Go and write them and send them to me. So he wrote: May I be your ransom, a man was overcome by fear of Allah, may He be exalted, such that he abandoned women and good food, and he could not raise his head to the sky, and as for clothes, doubt was cast upon them. So he wrote: As for your words about leaving women, you know what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had of women, and as for your words about leaving good food, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to eat meat and honey, and as for your words that fear entered him until he could not raise his head to the sky, then he should increase in reciting these verses: 'The patient, the truthful, the obedient, those who spend, and those who seek forgiveness by dawn.'

en.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi highlights the balance between reverence (khushu') and moderation in worship, as taught by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to Sukayn al-Nakhai. The Imam corrects Sukayn's extreme asceticism by citing the Prophet's consumption of meat and honey, demonstrating that permissible pleasures are not to be abandoned out of excessive fear. He recommends reciting Surah Al Imran, verse 17, to cultivate the virtues of patience, truthfulness, and night prayer, thereby grounding piety in balanced practice rather than ascetic withdrawal.
en.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on excessive asceticism and abandoning permissible pleasures out of fear of God?

key_terms.سُكَيْنُ النَّخَعِيُّ: Sukayn al-Nakhai, a companion of the Imams known for his piety and asceticism.
key_terms.الْخَوْفُ مِنَ اللَّهِ: Fear of God, a spiritual state that can lead to either humility or excessive anxiety.
key_terms.الصَّابِرِينَ وَالصَّادِقِينَ: The patient and the truthful, attributes mentioned in the Quranic verse.
key_terms.بِالْأَسْحَارِ: By dawn/early morning, referring to the time of night prayer and supplication.
